==Overall team records==
In this ranking [[Three points for a win|3 points are awarded for a win]], 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss. As per statistical convention in football, matches decided in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-outs]] are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co1110/records-all-time-table/|title=Women World Cup » All-time league table|website=worldfootball.net|access-date=3 July 2021}}</ref>

==Comprehensive team results by tournament==
;Legend
*{{bg|gold|1st}} – Champions
*{{bg|silver|2nd}} – Runners-up
*{{bg|#cc9966|3rd}} – Third place
*{{bg|#9acdff|4th}} – Fourth place
*QF – Quarter-finals
*R2 – Round 2 (2015–present: knockout round of 16)
*R1 – Round 1 (1991–present: group stage)
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;•&nbsp;}} – Did not qualify
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;••&nbsp;}} – Qualified but withdrew 
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;•×&nbsp;}} – Withdrew during qualification / Disqualified during qualification (after playing matches)
*{{border|width=1px|color=gray|&nbsp;×&nbsp;}} – Did not enter / Banned
*{{border|width=3px|color=red|&nbsp;&nbsp;}} – Hosts
*Q – Qualified for forthcoming tournament

For each tournament, the number of teams in each finals tournament are shown (in parentheses).

==Teams: tournament position==
Teams having equal quantities in the tables below are ordered by the tournament the quantity was attained in (the teams that attained the quantity first are listed first). If the quantity was attained by more than one team in the same tournament, these teams are ordered alphabetically.

; Most titles won: 4: {{fbw|USA}} (1991, 1999, 2015, 2019).
; Most finishes in the top two: 5: {{fbw|USA}} (1991, 1999, 2011, 2015, 2019).
; Most finishes in the top three: 8: {{fbw|USA}}  (1991–2019).
; Most finishes in the top four: 8: {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2019).
; Most finishes in the top eight: 8: {{fbw|GER}}, {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2019).
; Most World Cup appearances: 9: {{fbw|BRA}}, {{fbw|GER}}, {{fbw|JPN}}, {{fbw|NGA}}, {{fbw|NOR}}, {{fbw|SWE}}, {{fbw|USA}} (every tournament).
; Most second-place finishes: 1: {{fbw|NOR}} (1991), {{fbw|GER}} (1995), {{fbw|CHN}} (1999), {{fbw|SWE}} (2003), {{fbw|BRA}} (2007), {{fbw|USA}} (2011), {{fbw|JPN}} (2015), {{fbw|NED}} (2019), {{fbw|ENG}} (2023).
; Most third-place finishes: 4:  {{fbw|SWE}} (1991, 2011, 2019, 2023).
; Most fourth-place finishes: 2: {{fbw|GER}} (1991, 2015), {{fbw|NOR}} (1999, 2007).
; Most 3rd-4th-place finishes: 4: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991, 2011, 2019, 2023).
; Most 5th-8th-place finishes: 4: {{fbw|CHN}} (1991, 2003, 2007, 2015).
; Most 9th-16th-place finishes: 7: {{fbw|NGA}} (1991, 1995, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2019, 2023).

===Consecutive===
; Most consecutive championships: 2:  {{fbw|GER}} (2003–2007), {{fbw|USA}} (2015–2019).
; Most consecutive finishes in the top two: 3: {{fbw|USA}} (2011–2019).
; Most consecutive finishes in the top three: 8: {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2019).
; Most consecutive finishes in the top four: 8: {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2019).
; Most consecutive finishes in the top eight: 8: {{fbw|GER}}, {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2019).
; Most consecutive appearances in the finals: 9: {{fbw|BRA}}, {{fbw|GER}}, {{fbw|JPN}}, {{fbw|NGA}}, {{fbw|NOR}}, {{fbw|SWE}}, {{fbw|USA}} (1991–2023).
; Most consecutive championships by a confederation: 2: [[UEFA]] (2003–2007), [[CONCACAF]] (2015–2019).

===Gaps===
; Longest gap between successive titles: 16 years: {{fbw|USA}} (1999–2015).
; Longest gap between successive appearances in the top two: 12 years: {{fbw|USA}} (1999–2011).
; Longest gap between successive appearances in the top three: 12 years: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991–2003).
; Longest gap between successive appearances in the top four: 12 years: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991–2003).
; Longest gap between successive appearances in the top eight: 28 years: {{fbw|ITA}} (1991–2019).
; Longest gap between successive appearances in the finals: 20 years: {{fbw|ITA}} (1999–2019).

===Host team===
; Best finish by host team: Champion: {{fbw|USA}} (1999).
; Worst finish by host team: Group Stage: {{fbw|NZL}} (2023).

===Defending champion===
; Best finish by defending champion: Champion: {{fbw|GER}} (2007), {{fbw|USA}} (2019).
; Worst finish by defending champion: Round of 16: {{fbw|USA}} (2023).

===Debuting teams===
; Best finish by a debuting team: Champion: {{flagicon|USA}} [[United States women's national soccer team|United States]] (1991).
; Best finish by a debuting team, excluding inaugural tournament: Quarterfinals: {{fbw|ENG}} (1995), {{fbw|RUS}} (1999)

; Most finishes in the top three without ever being champion: 5: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991, 2003, 2011, 2019, 2023).
; Most finishes in the top four without ever being champion: 5: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991, 2003, 2011, 2019, 2023).
; Most finishes in the top eight without ever being champion: 7: {{fbw|SWE}} (1991–2003, 2011, 2019, 2023).

; Most finishes in the top eight without ever finishing in the top two: 4: {{fbw|AUS}} (2007–2015, 2023), {{fbw|FRA}} (2011–2023).
; Most appearances without ever finishing in the top two: 9: {{fbw|NGA}} (every tournament).
; Most finishes in the top eight without ever finishing in the top four: 2: {{fbw|DEN}} (1991–1995), {{fbw|RUS}} (1999–2003), {{fbw|ITA}} (1991, 2019).
; Most appearances without ever finishing in the top four: 9: {{fbw|NGA}} (every tournament).

; Most players scoring at least seven goals in a tournament: 2: 1991 ([[Michelle Akers]] ({{fbw|USA}}), [[Heidi Mohr]] ({{fbw|GER}})), 1999 ([[Sissi (footballer)|Sissi]] ({{fbw|BRA}}), [[Sun Wen (footballer)|Sun Wen]] ({{fbw|CHN}})).

==Coaching==
; Most matches coached: 25:<ref name=Paulo>{{Cite web |url=http://resources.fifa.com/mm/document/fifafacts/womcompwwc/02/60/95/85/stats_kit_4_players_neutral.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150605040832/http://resources.fifa.com/mm/document/fifafacts/womcompwwc/02/60/95/85/stats_kit_4_players_neutral.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 June 2015 |title=Statistical Kit - FIFA Women's World Cup Canada 2015 |publisher=FIFA|accessdate=6 June 2015}}</ref> [[Even Pellerud]] ({{fbw|NOR}}, 1991–1995, 2015; {{fbw|CAN}}, 2003–2007).
; Most matches won: 16: [[Even Pellerud]] ({{fbw|NOR}}, 1991–1995, 2015; {{fbw|CAN}}, 2003–2007).
; Most matches lost: 9: [[Tom Sermanni]] ({{fbw|AUS}}, 1995, 2007–2011; {{fbw|NZL}}, 2019).
; Most finals won: 2: [[Jill Ellis]] ({{fbw|USA}}, 2015–2019).
; Most finals lost: 2: [[Sarina Wiegman]] ({{fbw|NED}}, 2019; {{fbw|ENG}}, 2023).
; Most tournaments: 5:<ref name=Paulo/> [[Even Pellerud]] (1991–1995, 2003–2007, 2015).
; Most different nations coached: 3: [[Pia Sundhage]] ({{fbw|USA}}, 2011; {{fbw|SWE}}, 2015; {{fbw|BRA}}, 2023).
; Most consecutive tournaments with same team: 3: [[Silvia Neid]] ({{fbw|GER}}, 2007–2015).
; Youngest coach: {{Age in years, months and days|1989|02|05|2015|06|08}}:<ref name=ecu>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/womensworldcup/news/y=2015/m=3/news=89-days-to-go-2556627.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150310012250/http://www.fifa.com//womensworldcup/news/y=2015/m=3/news=89-days-to-go-2556627.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 March 2015 |title=89 days to go |publisher=FIFA|accessdate=9 March 2015}}</ref> [[Vanessa Arauz]] ({{fbw|ECU}}), vs [[Cameroon women's national football team|Cameroon]], 8 June 2015.
; Youngest coach, champions: {{Age in years, months and days|1951|4|9|1991|11|30}}: [[Anson Dorrance]] ({{fbw|USA}}), 1991.
; Oldest coach: {{Age in years, months and days|1951|06|21|2023|08|01}}: [[Mai Đức Chung]] ({{fbw|VIE}}), vs [[Netherlands women's national football team|Netherlands]], 1 August 2023.
; Oldest coach, champions: {{Age in years, months and days|1958|5|24|2011|7|17}}: [[Norio Sasaki]] ({{fbw|JPN}}), 2011.
; Quickest substitution made: 6th minute:  [[Chong Tsu-pin]] ({{fbw|TPE}}), [[Hong Li-chyn]] for [[Liu Hsiu-mei]], vs [[Nigeria women's national football team|Nigeria]], 1991;  [[Marika Domanski-Lyfors]] ({{fbw|SWE}}), [[Therese Lundin (footballer)|Therese Lundin]] for [[Hanna Ljungberg]], vs [[Ghana women's national football team|Ghana]], 1999.
; Most finals appearances as player and head coach: 6: [[Martina Voss-Tecklenburg]], {{flagcountry|GER}} (1991, 1995 & 1999 as player; 2015, 2019 & 2023 as coach).
; First person to have played and coached at the finals: [[April Heinrichs]], was the first person to have had both roles – as player for United States in 1991 and later as coach in 2003.
; Best performance by a foreign coach: A foreign coach has never managed a World Cup-winning team. The best performance by a team with a foreign coach is second place, reached by the United States in 2011 with [[Pia Sundhage]] of Sweden and England in 2023 with [[Sarina Wiegman]] of the Netherlands. The USA's coach for their 2015 and 2019 victories, [[Jill Ellis]], was born and spent her early childhood in England, but moved to the U.S. with her family at age 14, and had been a U.S. citizen for many years before becoming head coach in 2014.
